Here’s an advanced Keras project using hyperparameter tuning (Bayesian+Hyperband) on CIFAR‑10 classification—a significant step beyond standard model training:

Project Title

ai-ml-ds-TyN8PqZfLm — Hyperparameter-Optimized Deep CNN with Ensemble via Keras Tuner

Filename: hyperopt_deep_cifar10.py

🔍 Short Description

Build a deep CNN on CIFAR‑10 using Keras functional API, optimize architecture and training hyperparameters via Bayesian+Hyperband tuner, then ensemble best models for improved accuracy. Ultra‑advanced, optimized, and modular for production pipelines.

# hyperopt_deep_cifar10.py

import tensorflow as tf
import keras_tuner as kt
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers
from typing import Tuple

def load_data() -> Tuple[tf.data.Dataset, tf.data.Dataset]:
    (x_train, y_train), (x_test, y_test) = keras.datasets.cifar10.load_data()
    x_train = x_train.astype("float32") / 255.0
    x_test = x_test.astype("float32") / 255.0
    train_ds: tf.data.Dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_train, y_train)).shuffle(10000).batch(64).prefetch(1)
    test_ds: tf.data.Dataset = tf.data.Dataset.from_tensor_slices((x_test, y_test)).batch(64).prefetch(1)
    return train_ds, test_ds

def build_model(hp: kt.HyperParameters) -> keras.Model:
    inputs: layers.Input = keras.Input(shape=(32,32,3))
    x = inputs
    for i in range(hp.Int("conv_blocks", 2, 4, default=3)):
        filters: int = hp.Int(f"filters_{i}", 32, 128, step=32, default=64)
        for _ in range(2):
            x = layers.Conv2D(filters, (3,3), padding="same", activation="relu")(x)
            if hp.Choice(f"batchnorm_{i}", [True, False]):
                x = layers.BatchNormalization()(x)
        x = layers.MaxPooling2D()(x)
    x = layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D()(x)
    x = layers.Dense(hp.Int("dense_units", 64, 256, step=64, default=128), activation="relu")(x)
    x = layers.Dropout(hp.Float("dropout_rate", 0.2, 0.5, step=0.1, default=0.3))(x)
    outputs = layers.Dense(10, activation="softmax")(x)

    model = keras.Model(inputs, outputs)
    model.compile(
        optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(hp.Float("lr", 1e-4, 1e-2, sampling="log", default=1e-3)),
        loss="sparse_categorical_crossentropy",
        metrics=["accuracy"]
    )
    return model

def run_tuning():
    train_ds, test_ds = load_data()
    tuner = kt.Hyperband(
        build_model,
        objective="val_accuracy",
        max_epochs=20,
        factor=3,
        directory="tuner_dir",
        project_name="cifar10_kerastuner"
    )
    stop_early = tf.keras.callbacks.EarlyStopping(monitor="val_loss", patience=3)
    tuner.search(train_ds, validation_data=test_ds, callbacks=[stop_early])
    best_hps = tuner.get_best_hyperparameters(num_trials=3)
    models = [tuner.hypermodel.build(hp) for hp in best_hps]

    # Fine-tune each best model
    histories = []
    for model in models:
        histories.append(model.fit(train_ds, epochs=10, validation_data=test_ds))
    return models

def ensemble_predict(models, x: tf.Tensor) -> tf.Tensor:
    preds = [model.predict(x) for model in models]
    avg = tf.reduce_mean(tf.stack(preds, axis=0), axis=0)
    return tf.argmax(avg, axis=1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import numpy as np
    models = run_tuning()
    (_, _), (x_test, y_test) = tf.keras.datasets.cifar10.load_data()
    x_test = x_test.astype("float32") / 255.0
    y_pred = ensemble_predict(models, x_test)
    acc: float = np.mean(y_pred.numpy().flatten() == y_test.flatten())
    print(f"Ensemble Test Accuracy: {acc:.4f}")

🧪 Example Use Cases

  • Quick run → Print ensemble accuracy above.
  • Single image inference: img: tf.Tensor = x_test[:1] # shape [1,32,32,3] pred: tf.Tensor = ensemble_predict(models, img) print("Predicted class:", int(pred.numpy()[0]))
